reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the premise that edge dislocations can dominate high-temperature deformation in some refractory HEAs, but it does not provide evidence for the effects of SRO, the specific annealing treatment, or the link between SRO-enhanced lattice distortions and improved mechanical stability. The key premises about SRO and its mechanistic role are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Edge dislocations dominate high-temperature plasticity in some refractory BCC HEAs, contrary to conventional BCC alloys
Lattice distortions from chemical complexity enhance barriers for edge dislocation motion
Short-range ordering (SRO) increases local lattice distortions without forming secondary phases
Enhanced lattice distortions from SRO further impede edge dislocation glide, stabilizing yield strength and elastic moduli at high temperature
The proposed annealing treatment (~850°C) promotes SRO in NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 while maintaining single-phase BCC structure
